title: The 'Earth Loses Gravity' Hoax, Explained
description:
A viral claim said Earth would lose gravity for 7 seconds on August 12, 2026, and that NASA spent $89 billion preparing for it. Neither is true. Here's where the hoax actually came from, and why gravity can't do what the claim says.

Sources: NASA's public statement debunking the claim; reporting from Newskarnataka and VT.co tracing the hoax's origin to a 2020 hypothetical video by the YouTube channel What If.

#shorts #sciencefacts #mythbusting

scenes.text: In August 2026, a claim went viral that Earth would lose gravity for exactly seven seconds. Here's what actually happened.
The claim said NASA spent eighty nine billion dollars on a secret project called Operation Anchor, just to survive it.
NASA never confirmed any of this, because none of it is real. There is no Operation Anchor, and no such budget.
Gravity also isn't the kind of thing that can just pause. It's not a switch, it's the shape spacetime takes because mass exists.
The hoax traces back to a 2020 video by the channel What If, which explored gravity vanishing as a pure thought experiment, not a prediction.
August twelfth came and went. Nothing happened, because nothing was ever going to. Always check who's actually making the claim.
